scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to delete their stepbrother's profile on their Nintendo Switch. Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, the person had to watch their stepbrother for a week because their dad and his mom went on a trip. They brought their Nintendo Switch along because they wanted something to do during their long train commute to school. The stepbrother wanted to play on it, and it actually helped distract him while the person studied. So, to prevent the stepbrother from messing up their saves, they created a new profile for him on the Switch. When they got back to school, they got annoyed because every time they started a game or went to the eShop, they had to click on their own profile. So, they decided to delete the stepbrother's profile. Now, during Thanksgiving, when the stepbrother tried to play, he found out his Zelda save was gone and got upset, even crying a little. The dad thinks it was mean, but the person didn't think it was a big deal since they usually don't bring the Switch over when visiting. Hmm, so the main issue here is deleting someone else's profile on a personal device, which led to the loss of their saved game. The person felt annoyed by having to switch profiles, but the stepbrother was emotionally affected by losing his progress. I think it's important to consider a few things here: ownership, boundaries, and empathy. The Nintendo Switch is the person's device, so they have the right to manage profiles on it. However, deleting someone else's profile without discussing it first might be seen as unfair, especially if that person was using it with permission. The stepbrother was using the Switch with the person's consent, and they even created a profile for him to prevent issues. So, there was an understanding that he could use it. Deleting his profile without telling him could be seen as breaking that trust. Also, the stepbrother was emotionally affected by losing his saved game. Games can be a significant investment of time and effort, and losing progress can be frustrating and upsetting. The person's action led to the stepbrother feeling upset, which is a negative outcome. On the other hand, the person felt annoyed by having to switch profiles every time they used the Switch. It's valid to want convenience, but there might have been other ways to address that annoyance without deleting the profile. For example, they could have discussed the issue with the stepbrother and found a compromise, like keeping the profile but making it less intrusive. Another angle is the concept of shared use of personal devices. While the Switch is the person's device, allowing someone else to use it creates a shared space. Deleting the profile without communication can be seen as asserting ownership in a way that disregards the shared use. Additionally, the dad's reaction adds another layer. The dad thinks it was mean, which suggests that from an external perspective, the action was perceived negatively. This reinforces the idea that the person's action might have been hurtful. In summary, while the person had the right to manage their device, deleting the profile without communication and causing emotional distress to the stepbrother seems unfair. It would have been better to discuss the issue and find a solution that respects both parties' needs.
